text:
anya: Heads-up: CI flagged auth/retry parity failing on the js/go sampleapps after a regen. Tests point to typehash churn from example key ordering.
regen-bot: regendiff: examples.UserCreate keys reordered -> typehash changed. See log: https://ci.internal/3311/logs/regen 
omar: I pushed a tiny openapi tidy that reordered example keys for readability. Didn't think it would affect typegen hashes.
kelly: The semver helper picked this up and suggested a minor->major bump because it treats any examples diff as API surface change. That's overzealous.
chris: We should canonicalize examples before hashing: stable-sort keys, normalize descriptions, strip non-semantic whitespace. Low-risk and prevents churn.
anya: Agree. Short-term: can we add a release-bot override to ignore this PR so publishing isn't blocked?
release-bot: acknowledged. I can skip semver suggestion for a single PR with an explicit flag.
omar: I'll revert the tidy in the sampleapp to get the publish out. Then open a proper fix for canonicalization.
kelly: Also adding a regen CI test that runs a reorder-only diff and asserts typehash unchanged. I'll draft it.
chris: Optionally add an allowlist in regen: `regen-ignore-list: examples-order-only` for repos that frequently mutate examples. But canonicalization is preferable.
anya: Plan: revert -> release-bot override -> canonicalize patch + CI test -> update semver heuristics. Assigning tasks: omar revert, chris canonicalize, kelly CI test.
omar: PR up for revert in 15m.
regen-bot: note: rerunning builds after revert recommended to clear stale artifacts.
anya: Thanks team, this has been a recurring friction point for onboarding DX. Let's also document in the devex playbook.
